decision.comment:
Evaluation stage completed with all pipeline-integrity checks passing (data audit: 10/10 checks green, zero train/val overlap, test not inspected per protocol, 8/8 search trials completed, test metrics locked during selection). No deterministic findings are present.

However, two significant performance observations warrant flagging:

1. **Large validation-to-test gap**: Validation accuracy reached 0.9952 (epoch 13) while test accuracy is 0.8951 — a ~10-point gap. Similarly, validation macro-F1 is 0.9953 vs test macro-F1 0.8713 (~12-point gap). The data audit confirms no train/val image overlap and the test set was not inspected during training, so this is not a confirmed leakage event. The most likely explanation is distribution shift: the test set (n=7180) appears to contain a harder or more diverse case mix than the validation set (n=10004). This is not a pipeline error but should be noted in any downstream reporting.

2. **Weak per-class performance on two classes**: Class 7 (cancer-associated stroma, support=421) has recall 0.525 and F1 0.651, with 80 samples misrouted to class 5 (smooth muscle) and 62 to class 2 (debris). Class 5 (smooth muscle, support=592) has precision 0.608 and F1 0.710, with 62 samples misrouted to class 1 (background) and 80 to class 7. These two classes form a confusion pair that accounts for the bulk of the test-set errors. This is a model-capacity/representation limitation rather than a pipeline defect.

The model-search anomaly artefact carries action='revise' / severity='warning', but its own comment confirms 8/8 trials completed with 0 failures and all protocol constraints met; the 'revise' flag appears to be a residual from an earlier review pass and does not indicate an unresolved defect at this stage.

No deterministic findings justify stopping. The pipeline is internally consistent: selection used validation-only metrics, test was locked, checkpoint and config hashes are present, and the training history shows monotonic val improvement with no overfitting signal during training (val loss also decreased). The val/test gap and class-7 weakness are model-quality observations, not integrity violations. Recommend proceeding, with a note that the 0.895 test accuracy and the class-5/7 confusion pair should be highlighted in any final summary.
issues: Val/test accuracy gap of ~10 points (0.9952 val vs 0.8951 test) suggests distribution shift between validation and test sets; not a confirmed leakage event (data audit passed) but warrants explicit disclosure in final reporting.
Class 7 (cancer-associated stroma) recall is 0.525 and F1 0.651; 80/421 samples misclassified as class 5 (smooth muscle) and 62 as class 2 (debris).
Class 5 (smooth muscle) precision is 0.608 and F1 0.710; 62/592 samples misclassified as class 1 (background) and 80 as class 7. The class-5/class-7 confusion pair is the dominant error source.

anomaly_model_search artefact carries action='revise' and severity='warning' despite its own comment confirming successful completion (8/8 trials, 0 failures); residual flag should be cleared or explicitly acknowledged to avoid confusion in downstream stages.
